content.title: About
content.content: Yeast are single‑cell fungi used in cooking, brewing, and baking for fermentation. The most common type is the brewer’s yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae. They convert sugars into carbon dioxide and alcohol, making dough rise and giving beverages their alcoholic character.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Yeast have been used by humans for more than 7,000 years; the earliest archaeological evidence comes from ancient Egypt.
There are over 1,500 yeast species, but only a few dozen are employed in food production.
Yeast can survive extreme conditions, tolerating high sugar, salt, and alcohol concentrations.
In 1928, Elie Willyard discovered yeast as a model organism for genetics, paving the way for modern molecular biology.
Dry yeast is sold as granules, allowing it to stay active for up to two years at room temperature.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Yeast provide thiamine, riboflavin, niacin, and folate, which support energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Dry yeast contains about 40 % protein, including all essential amino acids, making it a valuable addition to vegetarian diets.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Yeast are a source of iron, zinc, magnesium, and selenium, important for immunity and metabolic processes.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Beta‑glucans in yeast promote the growth of beneficial gut bacteria and may improve digestive health.

items.title: May lower cholesterol
items.content: Studies suggest regular consumption of yeast powder can reduce total cholesterol and LDL levels.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to yeast, ranging from skin rashes to swelling and breathing difficulties.

items.title: High purine content
items.content: Yeast are rich in purines, which can increase uric acid production and may be problematic for people with gout.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Dry yeast is often fortified with salt; those limiting sodium should choose unsalted varieties.

items.title: Excessive intake
items.content: Large amounts can cause gastrointestinal upset, such as gas, bloating, and diarrhea.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Yeast can be added to bread, rolls, and pizza dough, sprinkled over finished dishes, used in sauces and soups, or dissolved in water or juice as a nutritious drink. Dry yeast is typically sold as a powder, making it easy to store and dose.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry yeast in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. After opening, keep it in the refrigerator, where it remains active for up to 12 months. Discard yeast that smells moldy or feels damp.
